native_result.query: The effect of which variable on BA degree completion decreases from 0.5024 to 0.0923 (while becoming insignifcant) when both SES and academic characteristics are included in analysis?
native_result.HypoA: The effect of SES on BA degree completion decreases from 0.3636  (significant) to  -0.2293 (insignificant) and effect of race on BA degree completion decreases from 0.5024  (significant) to 0.0923 (insignificant) when academic characteristics are considered.
native_result.HypoB:
EXECUTION COMPLETE.

ANSWER / HYPOTHESIS (data-grounded):
The variable is RACE (race/ethnicity). The association of being Black or Hispanic (relative to White) with BA degree completion is strong and significant in the univariate model but shrinks by roughly 5–6× and becomes statistically non-significant once SES and academic characteristics (ASVAB ability composite + percentile-in-class) are added — i.e., the racial/ethnic gap in BA completion is largely explained by socioeconomic status and academic preparation. In this subset the single cleanest dummy match is the BLACK (vs. White) category, with Hispanic showing the same direction and also losing significance.

- Only the race dummies both (a) are significant in Model A and (b) become non-significant in Model B (Black p .000→.54; Hispanic p .003→.26) with a several-fold shrinkage.

- The literal 0.5024/0.0923 are not reproduced in this subset; the match is by pattern (variable, direction, ~5× shrinkage, loss of significance), not exact value.
